steps.what: Analyse system requirements, capacity, cost evidence and customer needs
Determine project feasibility and explain constraints, uncertainties and required further evidence

tasks.design: Retain feasibility analysis and judgement with the engineer using evidence in {DOCS} and existing calculation sheets in {SPREADSHEET}. No saving is assigned to existing arithmetic or to a generated feasibility verdict.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feasibility depends on uncertain requirements, physical limits and commercial assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing analysis tools help organise evidence but do not establish removal of the engineering judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete customer needs, uncertain capacity and costs that depend on unresolved design choices.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising which assumptions could reverse the feasibility conclusion.
tasks.altitude: The engineer retains feasibility responsibility and gains no new investment authority.

reach.task: Explain feasibility conditions that must be resolved before commitment
reach.learn: Decision assumptions and project risk ownership

evidence.claim: Electronics feasibility depends on engineering and commercial assumptions; no labour saving from replacing that judgement is established.

assumptions: Boundary is feasibility analysis and its conclusion, excluding producing a detailed design, supplier pricing negotiations and sponsor investment approval.

The customer supplies needs, the requirements owner supplies current requirements, and existing technical/cost owners supply available evidence before s1. The engineer clarifies and records assumptions within the fully retained analysis time.
No complete structured capacity or cost model is assumed. Missing evidence requires manual analysis or further investigation, not a generated feasible flag.
Use native calculation and requirements tools before custom systems; existing calculation runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because the feasibility process is unchanged.
research_questions: Which assumptions dominate the feasibility conclusion and what evidence could reverse it?

already_counted.description: Analysis and accountable feasibility judgement remain fully counted

incremental.description: No changed system or process to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Exact feasibility judgement, requirement/evidence versions and stated assumptions; changed evidence or assumptions require renewed engineering review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Scenario retains substantive feasibility analysis without inventing a separate report-composition baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and maintain engineering schedules and records

steps.what: Check source facts and author schedule decisions, design notes or operational report content
Prepare schedules, design documentation, reports or charts from the checked content
Review, maintain and release the exact engineering schedule, documentation or report version

tasks.design: Configure native templates and charts in {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET} to assemble engineer-checked content. The engineer still chooses maintenance timings, authors technical explanations and reviews revisions; only repeated formatting and copying are automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved content and source values may be copied into several engineering layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document fields, tables and charts can reuse explicit content without a model inventing technical meaning.
tasks.still_hard: Correct maintenance timing, design version alignment and reports that reflect actual operation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparently complete record is technically misleading or stale.
tasks.altitude: Less document assembly is possible while engineering content and revision responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain engineering source and revision traceability
reach.learn: Document status, versions and controlled distribution

evidence.claim: Deterministic assembly of checked engineering tables, text and charts is plausible; its local labour saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is routine engineering schedule/document/report preparation and maintenance, excluding design creation, physical maintenance and project-specific execution criteria. Shares represent a mix of document types, not a requirement to create all types for every case.

Before s1, equipment owners supply existing maintenance requirements, designers supply current design evidence and operations staff supply existing operating records. Those producer tasks are unchanged and not transferred.

In s1 the engineer checks or captures equipment/project ID, source/version, reporting period and required values/units, authors technical text and determines any maintenance activity, date, interval and responsible role. The engineer also specifies template, included records, chart axes/units and document version. All capture, authoring and schedule judgement remain counted.

S2 copies only the checked content and applies specified layouts; it does not choose maintenance intervals, derive design conclusions or infer missing operational values. Missing or conflicting data require manual preparation and review.
Test native templates and charts before custom code. Existing automated assembly earns no new saving. Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for template upkeep, source mappings and assembly faults.
research_questions: Does native assembly save time after content authoring, source-version checks and final technical review?

already_counted.description: Source capture, technical authoring and schedule judgement remain counted
Technical review, revision and release remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain templates and mappings and resolve assembly faults

approvals.approved_version: Exact engineering document version, source snapshot, schedule/content decisions and distribution target; changed content or sources void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross saving 25 less 8 upkeep gives net 17. Range 2-10 assumes repeated formatting/copying today while schedule judgement, technical authoring and document maintenance remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine project material or equipment needs from technical scope and available resources

tasks.design: Keep material and equipment needs determination with the engineer using {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the engineering design environment. Existing parts-list extraction can support the work but does not decide test equipment capability, suitability or unresolved project needs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs are not always a complete bill of materials and depend on technical choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing design records help reference known parts without establishing a new saving in requirement judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Special equipment capabilities, substitutions and project needs not yet captured in a design.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising missing resources and unsuitable substitutes.
tasks.altitude: The engineer retains technical resource-determination responsibility without gaining purchasing authority.

reach.task: Explain the technical constraints of a required component or instrument

evidence.claim: Determining project material and equipment suitability remains engineering judgement beyond extracting an existing parts list.

assumptions: Boundary is determining technical needs, excluding purchase ordering, stocktaking and supplier selection. Existing bill-of-materials runtime is not counted as human work removed.

Project/design owners provide existing scope and design evidence and equipment owners supply available resource information before s1. The engineer clarifies gaps and records needs within this fully retained step.
No complete structured bill of materials or equipment-suitability flag is assumed. Missing evidence requires manual technical clarification.
Test native design-record extraction before custom tools for any separately demonstrated list-administration problem.
Zero incremental upkeep because technical needs determination is unchanged.
research_questions: Which resource needs arise outside the existing parts list and require technical assessment?

already_counted.description: Technical material and equipment needs determination remains fully counted

incremental.description: No changed tool or procedure to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario retains actual technical needs determination and does not invent a separate copying baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare project criteria, procedures and plans

steps.what: Determine project criteria and technical requirements for preparation, validation, installation, quality or testing
Prepare the necessary project procedure, report or plan from checked criteria and notes

loop.purpose: Draft clear project-specific prose from engineer-determined criteria without inventing technical steps
loop.input: Checked project criteria and engineering procedure notes with source references and limitations
loop.output: Draft procedure, plan or report retaining explicit criteria and source links
loop.check: Engineer checks sequence, prerequisites, units, acceptance limits, responsibilities and unsupported assertions against the supplied notes and evidence
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing criteria or unsupported technical instructions return to manual authoring
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates should fill fixed sections first; varied explanatory prose may require a bounded drafting loop

steps.what: Verify the exact criteria and execution document and release within engineering authority

tasks.design: Use a native template and bounded drafting loop in {DOCS} to express engineer-determined criteria and execution notes. The engineer verifies and releases the exact document within existing authority; site readiness, safety and validation decisions are not inferred from completed prose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning engineering decisions into clear project-specific instructions takes writing time.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from a constrained, checked source pack is plausible with full engineering review.
tasks.still_hard: Correct acceptance criteria, real site conditions and whether the procedure is executable and adequate.
tasks.human_edge: Determining the technical criteria and identifying missing prerequisites before release.
tasks.altitude: The engineer may compose documents faster while retaining criteria, sequence and adequacy responsibility.

reach.task: Prepare traceable project criteria for specialist validation review
reach.learn: Evidence traceability, prerequisite checks and approval boundaries

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting from engineer-checked criteria is plausible; its engineering-specific accuracy and labour saving remain unmeasured.
Relatics supports requirements and verification records, providing a native-first option for traceability rather than evidence that generated project procedures are correct.

assumptions: Boundary is project-specific criteria and execution-document preparation, excluding routine maintained design/operational records, actual installation, testing and specialist validation approval. Overlapping document assembly is counted once in a roll-up.

Project, site and design owners supply existing evidence before s1. The engineer determines and records scope, prerequisites, criterion IDs, acceptance limits/units, rationale, intended sequence, responsibilities, evidence requirements and source versions in s1; all criteria creation and capture remain counted.
No structured acceptance limit or site-ready flag is assumed free. Missing evidence requires manual investigation; s2 cannot invent a test threshold, safety instruction or facility status.

Input preparation and draft correction stay in s2's retained time. S3 checks the final document and records any further approvals required by existing process; such specialist work is unchanged and not a new free transfer.
Test native templates and requirements records before custom drafting. Allow 5 focal hours per 100 baseline for instructions, source handling and sampled document audits.
unknowns: Existing criteria and site evidence quality
research_questions: Does checked-source drafting save time after prerequisite, sequence and acceptance-limit review?

already_counted.description: Criteria creation and source capture remain fully counted
Draft input preparation and correction remain counted
Final technical review and release remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and audit source-linked execution documents

approvals.approved_version: Exact project execution document, criteria and source versions, prerequisites and release scope; changed sequence, limits or evidence voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=87.75; gross saving 12.25 less 5 upkeep gives net 7.25. Range 0-5 assumes repeated prose composition remains but difficult criteria, source gaps and full engineering review limit returns.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Routine document assembly and checked-source prose may require less repetition; feasibility, resource suitability and project criteria remain accountable engineering decisions.
reach: Explain feasibility conditions to project managers
Prepare traceable execution criteria for validation specialists
Clarify component constraints for technical buyers
role.ambitious_version: Improve the consistency and traceability of project documents while retaining the engineering reasoning that determines whether a project and its procedures are sound.
